findings.summary: The site does not follow the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot is visually identical to the light surface; the existing Night theme is only activated manually.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map page surfaces and text to preference-aware colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while retaining the manual override.

findings.summary: Continuous decorative animation continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found seven running animations, including flare, four flashing border animations, blueFlow, and pulseGlow; no reduced-motion CSS rule was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove the repeating flare, border, gradient, blink, and scale animations or reduce them to an immediate state.

findings.summary: Page navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or @view-transition usage across the multi-page home-to-article journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with cross-document View Transitions and a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation is an ad-hoc hidden checkbox and labels rather than a semantic control.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows #menubtn plus label.menublabel controls a fixed panel; there is no button, dialog, popover, or details primitive, and the input could not receive programmatic focus.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real button with expanded/controls state and a semantic disclosure or popover pattern, preserving light dismiss and Escape behavior.

findings.summary: Repeated social-channel promotions crowd the primary sports content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show four large promotional rows before match information, consuming roughly 340px of the first mobile viewport and repeating on home, article, and contact templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse social promotion to one compact, secondary module after primary content and keep only the most valuable action in the first viewport.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and several controls are below recommended target height.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused links successfully but every sampled link computed outline: none and box-shadow: none. Control geometry also shows nav and social controls at 35px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and enlarge compact controls to at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels without relying on hover.

findings.summary: Key templates miss the good LCP threshold in lab tests.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 2.6s on home and article and 3.8s on contact; article time-to-interactive was 12.8s. The direct trace corroborated home LCP at 2.10s under a separate desktop run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the true LCP element, shorten server and dependency chains, and defer non-essential widgets so all representative templates stay at or below 2.5s.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking styles and synchronous third-party scripts lengthen the critical path.
findings.evidence: HAR plus DOM confirmation found two Font Awesome stylesheets in head and synchronous classic scripts for timer.js and widgets.365scores.com/main.js; Lighthouse flagged the network dependency tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate critical CSS, self-host or subset icons, and defer or conditionally load the timer and scores widget after primary content.

findings.summary: Third-party and duplicate code dominate the page load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 22 script requests and 406,812 script bytes. Two major Font Awesome versions load together, while 365scores creates 21 requests and GTM is the largest script at 134,970 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Load one icon implementation, audit tag-manager payloads, and lazy-load the scores widget only when its visible feature is needed.

findings.summary: Landmarks, list semantics, alt text, and link names are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found no main landmark on every template, malformed ul/li nesting, unnamed linked images on article/contact, and a contact image without alt text. Accessibility scores were 85, 81, and 73.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a main landmark; repair list ownership; give meaningful linked images names and informative images alt text, or mark decorative images appropriately.

findings.summary: Several action and metadata colors fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured white on WhatsApp green at 1.98:1, Instagram at 4.33:1, share controls as low as 2.46:1, and article metadata at 3.84:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken colored control backgrounds or use dark foreground text so normal text reaches 4.5:1 and essential UI boundaries remain visible.

findings.summary: Keyboard users receive no visible location cue.
findings.evidence: The active focus probe reports outline none and box-shadow none for every sampled visible link, while the global CSS resets outline to 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a consistent :focus-visible ring with sufficient contrast and verify tab order through header, social actions, match tabs, content, and footer.

findings.summary: Some interactive targets are too short for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The control-size probe found primary nav, social icons, day tabs, and footer links at 35px or 15px high, below the commonly recommended 44px target. Reflow itself had no overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes with padding or min-block-size while retaining the proven 360px no-overflow layout.

findings.summary: Every tested template throws a JavaScript syntax error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured SyntaxError: Unexpected token ) on home, article, and contact mobile documents.
findings.suggestedFix: Locate the malformed inline/generated script at the reported mobile-template location, correct the unmatched token, and add a console-error smoke test.

findings.summary: Images are distorted or missing intrinsic sizing.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all three home images missing a complete width/height pair, two oversized images, and no responsive source sets. Lighthouse found the article preview displayed at 2.36:1 despite a 3.00:1 source ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Supply width and height, preserve aspect-ratio/object-fit, and request correctly sized responsive Blogger image variants with srcset/sizes.

findings.summary: Page descriptions are generic rather than template-specific.
findings.evidence: Article and contact pages reuse the homepage description about news, wallpapers, scoreboards, and TV lists instead of describing the match or contact route.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise unique meta description for each article and static page from its visible purpose.

findings.summary: Article structured data contains placeholders and inaccurate fields.
findings.evidence: The article NewsArticle JSON-LD says headline "Article headline", uses example.com image URLs, and contains an unresolved author-photo substitution; homepage BlogPosting data also contains unresolved template text.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate valid page-specific NewsArticle JSON-LD from visible content, use real absolute image/logo URLs, and validate all substitutions before publishing.

findings.summary: HTTPS is present but key defenses and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no CSP or HSTS. All three analytics cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None, including a 400-day _ga cookie.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and a restrictive CSP, then set analytics cookies Secure with an appropriate SameSite value and only the necessary lifetime.

findings.summary: The page sends most requests and bytes to third parties without a visible privacy choice.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 33 of 41 requests and 606,421 of 702,185 transferred bytes as third-party. Tracker evidence found Google Analytics and Tag Manager plus ten third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove non-essential trackers, gate analytics on an appropriate consent/legal basis, minimize collected events, and load external widgets only on demand.

findings.summary: Clickjacking, referrer, and capability policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response has no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, no Referrer-Policy, and no Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, a strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy at the edge or origin.

findings.summary: The stylesheet is heavily tied to physical left/right directions.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM reports lang=en and dir=ltr, but CSS evidence contains extensive float:left/right, margin-left/right, padding-right, and positioned left/right declarations rather than logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep correct lang/dir and migrate layout rules to inline/block logical properties so translated and RTL variants do not require duplicate overrides.

findings.summary: Match dates and times are hard-coded instead of formatted for the visitor.
findings.evidence: The article renders "20 July 2026", "12:30 AM IST", 11:00 PM for UAE, and 10:00 PM for Saudi Arabia, with no semantic time elements and no page-owned Intl formatting signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Store one unambiguous event instant and format date/time with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the user locale; retain optional venue or selected-zone context.

findings.summary: Time-zone presentation is incomplete and ambiguous.
findings.evidence: The match lists abbreviations or country flags for three hand-picked zones but no offset, zone identifier, conversion control, or user-local time; 7/19 elsewhere on the same page conflicts with 20 July.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an ISO instant plus IANA time zone, show the viewer local time by default, and label alternate zones explicitly with DST-safe conversion.

findings.summary: Oversized and non-responsive images waste transfer.
findings.evidence: Image evidence found a 1600px logo displayed at 200px and a 2340px preview displayed around 178px, both without srcset; one content image remains JPEG.
findings.suggestedFix: Request appropriately sized modern variants and provide srcset/sizes plus intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: An empty match state still loads a large external scores application.
findings.evidence: The homepage says there are no important matches while 365scores makes 21 requests and transfers 257,559 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize the scores widget for an empty state; fetch it only after the user opens a live score surface or when matches exist.

findings.summary: Third-party resources are disproportionate to visible content.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 86% of transfer bytes, led by scores, tag manager, CDN icon assets, and analytics on a small content page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove duplicate icon libraries, defer the scores bundle, and measure each vendor against user value.
